result.source_concept: Version‑control bisect (binary search over code revisions)
result.target_concept: Debugging with breakpoints and step‑through execution

mappings.source_element: Checking out a version in the middle of history
mappings.target_element: Setting a breakpoint at a suspected code location
mappings.relation: Both serve as an initial narrowing point in the search for the fault
mappings.evidence: Analogy: 'checks out a version somewhere in the middle' ↔ Description: 'pauses the program's execution at a suspected location (a breakpoint)'

mappings.source_element: Repeatedly checking out earlier/later versions to narrow the range
mappings.target_element: Stepping through code line‑by‑line to narrow the range
mappings.relation: Iterative narrowing of the search space until the exact fault is isolated
mappings.evidence: Analogy: 'narrowing the search each time until it pinpoints the exact change' ↔ Description: 'step through the code line‑by‑line, narrowing the search until you pinpoint the exact instruction'

mappings.source_element: Identifying the specific change that introduced the bug
mappings.target_element: Identifying the specific line or logical flaw causing the failure
mappings.relation: Both represent the final pinpointed fault element
mappings.evidence: Analogy: 'once you find the specific change' ↔ Description: 'once you've found the specific line or logical flaw'

mappings.source_element: Running a quick test on the change and marking it good/bad
mappings.target_element: Inspecting internal state/variable values and deciding if execution is correct
mappings.relation: Evaluating the candidate point to determine if it is the source of the problem
mappings.evidence: Analogy: 'run a quick test on it... tell the tool whether that point is good or bad' ↔ Description: 'inspect its internal state and variable values'

result.process_summary: Both processes use an iterative, divide‑and‑conquer style search: they start at a midpoint, evaluate whether the fault lies before or after that point, and repeatedly halve the search space (or step forward) until the exact offending element—whether a code revision or a program instruction—is isolated, after which it can be examined and corrected.
potential_breaks: Version‑control bisect is a binary (logarithmic) search over discrete commits, whereas breakpoint debugging typically proceeds linearly rather than halving the code space
The analogy assumes an automated test that can label a revision as good or bad, while debugging relies on manual inspection of state
Changes in version history are immutable snapshots, while program execution state is mutable and may depend on runtime inputs
